reforms.description: The May 1985 federal budget reformed R&D tax incentives for private firms. It terminated the existing scientific research tax credit while simultaneously introducing enriched incentives for research and development to stimulate business fixed investment and support innovation capacity.
reforms.package_name: 1985 Federal Budget R&D Tax Incentive Reform
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The termination of the scientific research tax credit removes a growth-supporting incentive, but the introduction of enriched incentives is intended to stimulate business R&D investment and innovation capacity. The net effect depends on whether the new incentives are more generous or better-targeted than the old credit, which cannot be determined from the text alone.
reforms.status_evidence: Description [1] explicitly states 'The May 1985 federal budget provided enriched incentives', indicating implementation in the 1985 budget cycle. Description [0] states the credit was 'terminated', indicating the change took effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a significant reform of the R&D tax incentive system affecting private sector innovation, but it is narrower in scope than a system-wide restructuring and does not appear to be a major overhaul of the innovation support architecture.
reforms.source_quote: Enriched incentives for research and development were provided in the May budget.
